rag.description: Receive UDP datagrams in an automation to verify what an application or a device emitted. The step waits for a set number of datagrams, filters them by sender or content, and fails on a timeout, so a flow asserts network output as reliably as it asserts a screen.

qa.answer: It waits for UDP datagrams on a port or reads them from a started listener, and stores the message, its sender, and the full list.
qa.question: What does the ReceiveUdpMessage plugin do?

qa.answer: Listener or Port selects the source; Count and Timeout set how many datagrams to wait for and how long; RemoteHost, RemotePort, and Pattern filter them, and a datagram must match every filter set. The outputs are Message, MessageCount, Messages, RemoteAddress, and RemotePort.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of ReceiveUdpMessage?

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the download icon and the ActionRuleModel, usually after StartUdpListener and the action that makes the sender emit.
qa.question: How does ReceiveUdpMessage fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Start a listener before the triggering action instead of binding a Port afterwards, filter by sender on a busy port, and set a Timeout that covers the slowest expected sender.
qa.question: What are best practices for using ReceiveUdpMessage?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “ReceiveUdpMessage” and pass inputs in the argument, such as {{$ --Listener:Telemetry --Count:3 --Timeout:15000}}.
qa.question: How is a ReceiveUdpMessage rule configured?

qa.answer: The step fails with a timeout when fewer than Count matching datagrams arrive; a missing source, an unknown listener, port 0 or a port in use, an unknown format or encoding, an invalid Pattern, or an unresolved RemoteHost fails it before waiting; a listener another step stops before Count datagrams arrive, or a Pattern match longer than 30 seconds, fails it at once.

description: ### Purpose
ReceiveUdpMessage waits for UDP datagrams, single network messages, and stores what arrived.
It binds a port for the length of its own wait, or reads the buffer of a listener that was started earlier.
Flows use it to verify that an application or a device emitted the expected datagram, and to read its content.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Direct receive | Binds a port and waits for datagrams that arrive during the step. |
| Listener receive | Reads datagrams a started listener buffered while earlier steps ran. |
| Count and timeout | Waits for a set number of datagrams and fails the step when too few arrive in time. |
| Sender and content filters | Counts only datagrams that pass every filter set: sender host, sender port, and a text pattern. |
| Multicast | Joins a multicast group, an address many receivers share, for the length of a direct receive. |
| Text and binary output | Publishes datagrams as plain, hexadecimal, or Base64 text. |
| Message refinement | Reads one field of a JSON message, or one element or attribute of an XML message, and keeps a regular-expression match. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Device readings | Read a measurement a scale, sensor, or scanner sends over UDP. |
| Event triggers | Hold a flow, up to the timeout, until a system announces that a job finished. |
| Heartbeat monitoring | Confirm that a service still emits its periodic heartbeat. |
| Mock servers | Take a request on a listener and reply through the same listener with SendUdpMessage. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Emission checks | Assert that a UI action made the application send a telemetry or syslog datagram. |
| Content checks | Compare the fields of a received datagram with expected values. |
| Negative checks | Treat the timeout failure as the pass condition to prove that no matching datagram arrived. |
| Throughput checks | Require a number of datagrams within a time window. |
Stores the text of the first datagram, after OnElement, OnAttribute, and RegularExpression refined it.
The ResponseFormat argument selects plain, hexadecimal, or Base64 text.
entity.name: Message

description: Stores the number of datagrams the step collected.
Compare it with the expected number to tell a partial result from a full one.
entity.name: MessageCount

description: Stores every collected datagram as a JSON array, oldest first.
Each item holds `Data`, `Length`, `ReceivedAt`, `RemoteAddress`, and `RemotePort`.
entity.name: Messages

description: Stores the IP address of the sender of the first datagram.
Use it as the Host of a reply.
entity.name: RemoteAddress

description: Stores the port of the sender of the first datagram.
Use it as the Port of a reply.
entity.name: RemotePort

edge_cases: Datagram arrives before the step starts
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the datagram text in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Message` and its sender in `ReceiveUdpMessage:RemoteAddress` and `ReceiveUdpMessage:RemotePort`.
annotations.notes: A datagram that arrives before the step starts is lost, because no socket is bound yet. Use it for senders that repeat, such as a heartbeat.

description: ### Receive one datagram on a port
The step binds port 9100 and waits up to ten seconds for one datagram.
The socket closes when the step ends.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the oldest buffered datagram and removes it from the listener buffer.
annotations.notes: Start the listener before the action that makes the application send. The listener keeps what arrives while the steps in between run. Datagrams an earlier step took are no longer in the buffer.

description: ### Read a datagram a listener buffered
The Listener parameter reads from the listener named `Telemetry`.
The step returns at once when a datagram is already buffered, and waits up to five seconds otherwise.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the first datagram in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Message` and all three in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Messages`.
annotations.notes: The step fails when fewer than three arrive in time. The ones that did arrive stay in the buffer for a later read. A full buffer drops the oldest datagram first.

description: ### Wait for several datagrams
The Count parameter requires three datagrams within fifteen seconds.
The step returns as soon as the third one arrives.

edge_cases: Datagram from the host but another source port
Pattern is not a valid expression
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the first datagram from 192.168.1.50 port 5005 whose text starts with `ALARM`.
annotations.notes: Datagrams that do not match stay buffered. Another step can read them with its own filter.

description: ### Receive only a matching datagram from one sender
The RemoteHost and RemotePort parameters accept datagrams from one device and source port only.
The Pattern parameter accepts only text that starts with `ALARM`.

edge_cases: Group address is not an IP address
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the first datagram sent to the group on port 5000.
annotations.notes: The group is left when the step ends. Other receivers on the machine can share the port.

description: ### Receive a multicast datagram
The step binds port 5000 and joins the multicast group 239.255.0.1 on the interface 192.168.1.10.
It waits up to ten seconds for one datagram sent to the group.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the datagram as upper-case hexadecimal text without separators.
annotations.notes: Hexadecimal output keeps every byte of a binary packet visible for comparison. The default timeout of five seconds applies.

description: ### Receive a binary datagram as hexadecimal text
The ResponseFormat parameter publishes the bytes as hexadecimal text.
The step binds port 9100 and waits for one datagram.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the Latin1 text of the oldest buffered datagram in the session and leaves the response entity empty.
annotations.notes: Use the encoding of the sender, or accented letters are published as wrong characters. The session parameters stay available to later steps.

description: ### Read text in a legacy encoding and keep it out of the entity
The Encoding parameter reads the datagram bytes as Latin1 text.
The NoEntity switch publishes the outputs as session parameters only.

edge_cases: Field is missing from the datagram
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the value of `reading.value` in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Message`.
annotations.notes: Only the first datagram is refined. A datagram that is neither JSON nor XML keeps its whole text, and a missing field stores an empty value.

description: ### Read one field of a JSON datagram
The step reads a buffered JSON datagram and selects the `reading.value` field through the JSONPath in `onElement`.
The full datagram stays available in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Messages`.

edge_cases: Pattern is not a valid expression
annotations.expected_result: The step stores `21` in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Message` for the datagram `T=21;H=40`.
annotations.notes: The pattern runs on the whole text when onElement is not set. A pattern that does not match stores an empty value, and `ReceiveUdpMessage:Messages` keeps the full text.

description: ### Keep one value of a text datagram
The step reads the oldest buffered datagram, such as `T=21;H=40`.
A regular expression `(?<=T=)\d+` is applied to the value attribute and keeps the digits after `T=`.

edge_cases: Attribute is missing from the element
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the value of the `code` attribute in `ReceiveUdpMessage:Message`.
annotations.notes: Without onAttribute the step stores the markup of the whole element. A missing element or attribute stores an empty value.

description: ### Read one attribute of an XML datagram
The step reads the oldest buffered XML datagram and selects the `status` element through the XPath in `onElement`.
The `onAttribute` property keeps the value of its `code` attribute.
Stores the text of the first datagram, after OnElement, OnAttribute, and RegularExpression refined it.
The ResponseFormat argument selects plain, hexadecimal, or Base64 text. The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before comparing or displaying it.

description: Sets the number of matching datagrams the step waits for.
Defaults to 1, and the step fails when fewer arrive within Timeout, or sooner when another step stops the listener.
With a Listener, datagrams leave the buffer only when the full count arrived.
parameters.name: Count

description: Names the text encoding, such as `UTF8`, `ASCII`, `Unicode`, `UTF32`, `Latin1`, or a code page such as `windows-1252`.
Applies to datagrams published as text and to the Pattern filter.
Defaults to UTF-8, and a name the runtime does not know fails the step.
parameters.name: Encoding

description: Names a listener started by StartUdpListener and reads from its buffer.
Datagrams that arrived since the listener started and that no earlier step took are available, oldest first; a full buffer drops the oldest.
A name that is not started fails the step, and a listener another step stops during the wait fails it at once instead of with a timeout.
parameters.name: Listener

description: Binds one local IP address, which selects the network interface on a machine with several.
With MulticastGroup the step binds every interface and the address selects where the group is joined.
Defaults to every IPv4 interface, and is ignored when Listener is set.
parameters.name: LocalAddress

description: Joins a multicast group, such as `239.255.0.1`, for a step that binds its own Port.
Ignored when Listener is set, because a listener joins its own group, if any, when StartUdpListener starts it.
parameters.name: MulticastGroup

description: Leaves the response entity empty and publishes the outputs as session parameters only.
Use it when the datagram content must stay out of the extracted data of the flow.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Counts only datagrams whose text matches a regular expression, such as `^ALARM`.
The payload is read as text in the encoding of the step before matching.
Datagrams that do not match stay in the listener buffer for another step.
Combines with RemoteHost and RemotePort; an invalid expression fails the step before it waits, and a match that runs longer than 30 seconds fails it.
parameters.name: Pattern

description: Binds a local port, from 1 to 65535, for the length of the step; 0 fails the step, because no sender can know the port the system picks.
Only datagrams that arrive while the step waits are received, so use a Listener when the sender acts earlier.
Listener or Port is required, and Listener wins when both are set.
parameters.name: Port

description: Counts only datagrams sent from one host name or IP address.
Datagrams from other senders stay in the listener buffer for another step.
A host name is resolved once before waiting, and a name that does not resolve fails the step.
parameters.name: RemoteHost

description: Counts only datagrams sent from one source port, from 1 to 65535.
Defaults to 0, which accepts every source port.
parameters.name: RemotePort

description: Selects how the bytes of each datagram are published.
Defaults to Text, and any other value than Text, Hex, or Base64 fails the step.
parameters.name: ResponseFormat

description: Publishes each datagram as plain text in the encoding of the step.
Use it for text protocols and for JSON or XML payloads.
values.name: Text

description: Publishes each datagram as upper-case hexadecimal text without separators.
Use it to compare a binary packet byte by byte.
values.name: Hex

description: Publishes each datagram as Base64 text.
Use it to pass a binary packet to a later step without loss.
values.name: Base64

description: Sets how long to wait for the requested number of datagrams.
Accepts a number of milliseconds, such as `2000`, or a time span, such as `00:00:02`.
Defaults to 5000 milliseconds, which also replaces a value that is neither a number nor a time span.
parameters.name: Timeout

description: Holds the arguments of the step, such as `{{$ --Listener:Telemetry --Timeout:5000}}`.
Listener or Port is required.
properties.name: Argument

description: Names the locator type of the rule and stays at its default for this action.
The path in OnElement is read as JSONPath for JSON text and as XPath for XML text, whatever the value is.
properties.name: Locator

description: Names one attribute of the XML element that OnElement selects.
The attribute value replaces the element as the published text, and a missing attribute publishes an empty value.
Ignored for JSON text and when OnElement is empty.
properties.name: OnAttribute

description: Selects one part of the first datagram: a JSONPath such as `$.status` for JSON text, or an XPath such as `//status` for XML text.
The first result is kept: an XML element is published as its markup, and an attribute or a text node, such as `//status/@code`, as its value.
Text that is neither JSON nor XML skips the path, a path that finds nothing publishes an empty value, and a malformed path fails the step.
properties.name: OnElement

description: Keeps the first match of the pattern in the first datagram, after OnElement was applied.
Defaults to a pattern that keeps the whole text, and a pattern that does not match publishes an empty value.
properties.name: RegularExpression

summary: Waits for UDP datagrams, single network messages, on a port or reads them from a started listener, until a count or a timeout is reached.
Filters datagrams by sender address, sender port, or a text pattern, and fails the step when too few arrive.
Stores the message, its sender, and the full list, so a later step can assert what an application or device emitted.
